  "elsewhere_quote": "It follows that\n\\[\nb-c\\le \\frac{(t-y)^2}{4(t+c)}\\le \\frac{(t-y)^2}{4t}. \\tag{5}\n\\]",
  "status_as_written": "false_display",
  "repair_distance": "symbol",
  "explanation": "Expanding (t+2c+y)^2-4(t+c)(y+b) gives (t-y)^2+4c(t+c)-4b(t+c) = (t-y)^2+4(t+c)(c-b), so the displayed factor (b-c) is indeed a sign slip. However the very next line, (5), reads b-c \\le (t-y)^2/(4(t+c)), which is exactly the consequence of the correct expansion 0 \\le (t-y)^2+4(t+c)(c-b). The upper-inequality expansion and the telescoping in Section 3 use (5) in this correct form, so the Lipschitz-type bound (7) and the constancy of d — the necessity argument covering all t,y including fixed points — stand. A single symbol swap repairs the line.",
  "extra_notes": null
}
